explain: The tool or means goes in the ablative, with no preposition: _manū_ (by hand). _manus_ is fourth declension, so the ablative is _-ū_.
distractors: _manum_ is accusative. A means takes the ablative: _manū_.
_manus_ is nominative. A means takes the ablative: _manū_.
_manuī_ is dative. A means takes the ablative: _manū_.

explain: The sword is what he uses: the ablative of means, _gladiō_. No _cum_ is needed.
distractors: _gladium_ is accusative. A means takes the ablative: _gladiō_.
_gladius_ is nominative. A means takes the ablative: _gladiō_.
_gladiī_ is genitive or plural. A means takes the ablative: _gladiō_.
_tēla_ is nominative or accusative plural. A means takes the ablative: _tēlīs_.
_tēlōrum_ is genitive plural. A means takes the ablative: _tēlīs_.
_tēlum_ is singular and accusative. A means takes the ablative plural: _tēlīs_.

explain: How you do something is the ablative of manner, usually with _cum_: _cum cūrā_.
distractors: _cūrārum_ is genitive plural. _cum_ takes the ablative: _cūrā_.
_cūrae_ is genitive or dative. _cum_ takes the ablative: _cūrā_.

tag: magnā cum audāciā: with great boldness
explain: When the noun has an adjective, _cum_ can sit between them: _magnā cum audāciā_. Both words are ablative.
distractors: _audāciārum_ is genitive plural. _cum_ takes the ablative: _audāciā_.
_audāciae_ is genitive or dative. _cum_ takes the ablative: _audāciā_.

explain: _propter_ (because of) takes the accusative, not the ablative.
distractors: _īrae_ is genitive or dative. _propter_ takes the accusative: _īram_.
_īrās_ is plural accusative. One anger is singular: _īram_.

explain: A feeling that causes an action can stand alone in the ablative: _timōre_ (out of fear).
distractors: _timōrem_ is accusative. A cause takes the ablative: _timōre_.
_timor_ is nominative. A cause takes the ablative: _timōre_.
_timōrī_ is dative. A cause takes the ablative: _timōre_.

en: I come out of the city.
tag: ē urbe: out of the city
explain: _ē_ and _ex_ (out of) take the ablative. _ē_ is used before a consonant, _ex_ before a vowel.
Accompaniment takes _cum_ and the ablative: _cum amīcīs_.
distractors: _amīcī_ is nominative or genitive. _cum_ takes the ablative: _amīcīs_.

en: We do not live without water.
distractors: _aquārum_ is genitive plural. _sine_ takes the ablative: _aquā_.
_aquae_ is genitive or dative. _sine_ takes the ablative: _aquā_.

explain: _dē_ (about, down from) takes the ablative: _dē bellō_.
distractors: _bella_ is plural. _dē_ with one war takes _bellō_.
